rationale: ONNX's whole purpose is a framework-neutral model representation that PyTorch, TensorFlow, scikit-learn etc. export to and many runtimes/compilers/accelerators consume, which is a direct mechanism for the model and software-package interoperability RQ34 asks public compute infrastructure to ensure -- at the model-format layer, complementing kubeflow-trainer's training-runtime layer.

Federated training where each institution's raw data stays in place, protected by homomorphic encryption and MPC during joint computation -- a direct mechanism for reconciling data access with privacy-preserving ML, alongside flower and pysyft but with built-in cryptographic secure-aggregation and vertical (feature-partitioned) FL.

Implements MPC/HE secure computation across separate organisations, including vertical FL and private set intersection over parties holding different attributes of the same users -- a working mechanism for collaborative cross-entity analysis of user data without pooling it, RQ43's question.

Acts as an MLflow-compatible model registry: registered models with numbered model versions, storage locations and governed access, which is a concrete open implementation of the model-update tracking RQ56 asks about -- a catalog-level alternative to mlflow's own registry.

Specifies a standard, machine-readable set of lineage metadata (which job run consumed and produced which datasets, plus schema, ownership, data-quality and column-lineage facets) that data pipelines report as they run -- a concrete candidate reporting requirement for responsible data practice. Note: it does not cover licence metadata.

Gives every tool in a data/AI pipeline a common lineage event format, so a registry (e.g. Marquez, Egeria) can assemble end-to-end lineage across otherwise separate systems; this is the interchange layer that audit registries need for end-to-end tracing along the value chain, though verification still rests on the registry consuming the events.

Defines a structured, schema-validated contract that a data producer publishes alongside a dataset -- ownership, roles, intended purpose, usage limitations (technical, compliance, legal), links to licence agreements and privacy statements, quality rules and SLAs -- a concrete candidate licence/metadata reporting requirement for responsible data practice.

Its required and optional fields (schema, declared quality rules, purpose, usage, limitations, SLA, licence/terms references) are exactly the information a consumer needs to judge whether a dataset is fit for a given use such as training, an LF AI & Data standard alongside croissant and frictionless-data-package.

Its open metadata types define how licence and governance metadata attach to data assets (e.g. the License relationship records licence id, coverage dates, conditions, licensor, licensee and custodian), alongside certifications, classifications and governance definitions -- a concrete, implemented model for the licence and metadata reporting RQ7 asks about.

Federates metadata repositories across tools and organisations (open metadata repository cohorts) and stores lineage and governance metadata about assets, which is a working registry substrate for tracing assets end to end along a multi-party value chain.

monocle-test-tools evaluates agent behaviour on its execution trace rather than only input/output pairs -- asserting which tools were invoked with what arguments, whether responses match expectations, and error/cost states, including generated multi-turn scenario tests with simulated users -- a reusable mechanism for evaluating what an agent actually does.

Its trace assertions explicitly check which agents are invoked and whether they delegate tasks correctly across multi-agent frameworks (Google ADK, LangGraph, CrewAI), giving a concrete way to test interactions within a network of agents rather than one agent in isolation.
